## Claims
- [source-backed] For every bigrassmannian parameter tuple, the lower family \(\{\bar s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(i^j,b^a)\}\) generates \(J_v\), and no member can be removed. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 220-235]
- [source-backed] The homogeneous no-syzygy theorem used to prove lower-family minimality holds integrally in \(\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\). [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 819-831]
- [source-backed] The right family is the conjugate family \(\{\bar s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq((i+a)^b,i^{j-b})\}\), and its generation was proved in the transposed version. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 833-840]
- [proved] For \(i=j=3,\ a=2,\ b=3,\ r=n-r=5\), both displayed ten-element families map to \(\mathbb Z\)-bases of \(J/A_+J\).
- [proved] In the degreewise orders specified below, the transition from the lower basis to the right basis is \(\operatorname{diag}(1,-1,I_2,-I_2,I_2,-1,1)\), hence is unimodular.

## Strategy
Put \(A=\Lambda/I_{5,5}\). Since \(A\) is graded and \(h_t=\bar s_{(t)}=0\) for \(t>5\),
\[
A_+=(h_1,h_2,h_3,h_4,h_5).
\]
The lower family is
\[
\begin{array}{c|l}
d&\mathcal L_d\\ \hline
9&(333)\\
10&(3331)\\
11&(3332,33311)\\
12&(3333,33321)\\
13&(33331,33322)\\
14&(33332)\\
15&(33333).
\end{array}
\]
It generates \(J\). If a nonzero integral relation among its degree-\(d\) classes held in \(J/A_+J\), lifting it gives a homogeneous syzygy with a nonzero constant-coefficient left side and positive-degree multiples of lower-degree lower-family elements on the right. This is excluded by the cited integral no-syzygy theorem. Thus the displayed classes are independent; generation gives spanning. Hence they are a \(\mathbb Z\)-basis.

Let \(\omega(\bar s_\lambda)=\bar s_{\lambda'}\). It is a graded involution of \(A\), preserves \(A_+\), and maps the lower family to the right family. Since both families generate \(J\), \(\omega(J)=J\), so it induces an automorphism of \(J/A_+J\). Therefore the right-family classes are also a \(\mathbb Z\)-basis.

Write
\[
L_\rho=\bar s_{(3^3,\rho)},\qquad
R_{\rho'}=\bar s_{(3+\rho'_1,\,3+\rho'_2,\,3+\rho'_3)}
=\omega(L_\rho),
\quad \rho\subseteq3^2.
\]
The finite Pieri–antipode reduction gives
\[
[R_{\rho'}]=(-1)^{|\rho|}[L_\rho]\quad\text{in }J/A_+J.
\]
It follows by expanding the antipode identity
\[
\sum_{\alpha,\beta}(-1)^{|\alpha|}
c_{\alpha,\beta}^{\nu}s_{\alpha'}s_\beta=0
\]
and discarding each term in \(A_+J\); this is the integral Hopf-antipode identity used in the source proof. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 702-735]

Explicitly, the paired reductions are
\[
\begin{array}{c|c}
R&\text{class in the lower basis}\\ \hline
333& L_{0}\\
433&-L_{1}\\
443& L_{2}\\
533& L_{11}\\
444&-L_{3}\\
543&-L_{21}\\
544& L_{31}\\
553& L_{22}\\
554&-L_{32}\\
555& L_{33}.
\end{array}
\]
Thus, by degree \(9,\ldots,15\), the transition matrices are
\[
[1],\ [-1],\ I_2,\ -I_2,\ I_2,\ [-1],\ [1].
\]
Each has determinant \(\pm1\). The requested target is established.
